messages.subject: Estimating correlated residuals in only one of two groups
parts:
Hi group,

I am running a two-group measurement invariance investigation. I am trying to specify two correlated residuals, but I want the first one to apply only in group 1 and the second one to apply only in group 2.

Here is my model syntax WHICH DOES NOT WORK:
model1a <- '
 NFCf =~  N4r + N5r + N9r + N3r + N11 + N13 + N2 + N10 + N12r
 EXPf =~  R13 + R26 + R31 + R8 + R34 + R35 + R22 + R24r + R33
 DDf  =~  D8  + D28 + D31 + D14 + D17 + D20 + D2 + D5 + D25
 # adding correlated residuals
 D14 ~~ c(rD1,NA)*D20  #I want this only in group1
 R13 ~~ c(NA,rR2)*R8   #I want this only in group2
'

Any advice appreciated.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Estimating correlated residuals in only one of two groups
parts: I think Ed's first suggestion triggers more efficient optimization/estimation because the constraint is simpler:
NA means a parameter is free, as does assigning an unconstrained label. If you want a parameter estimate to be 0, use 0.

# adding correlated residuals
 D14 ~~ c(NA, 0)*D20  #I want this only in group1
 R13 ~~ c(0, NA)*R8   #I want this only in group2

A numeric vector is used for fixing parameters to a particular value, or freeing it with a missing value (NA).  A character vector is used to label parameters, which will be free by default, unless the same label (or a single label for multiple groups) is used to constrain those parameters to equality.

https://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/groups.html
